traits.height_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 466), Olneya: a tree reaching 9 m and a trunk 45 cm across, spiny branches, thin scaly bark; leaflets 8 to 24 (commonly 11 to 15), grey-hairy; pea flowers in short racemes, corolla about 12 mm, purple and white; foliage evergreen except in very cold winters; May and June. Their plate 15 shows a specimen near Gila Bend about 35 feet (10.7 m) high. So the tallest are 9 m by the text and 10.7 m by the plate.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Olneya tesota (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.92 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 2 records in 2 sources); trunks 0.92, branches 0.77. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long. Fitted so the tallest of five plants (seeds 1 to 5) stays within Jepson (1925): 4.57 m to 7.62 m tall. Once a leaf stayed one season, not two (leaf life, generator revision 44), more light reached the crown and, at 6.04, a plant reached 8.11 m.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a slow evergreen tree 5 to 10 m tall with a broad crown, smooth grey bark that shreds with age, short paired thorns, grey-green pinnate leaves and lavender pea flowers in late spring. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.bud_years.note: Short shoots leaf out for up to 40 years while they have light, as the other desert legume trees' are fitted to the Urban Tree Database (Olneya is not in it).

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card draws a cluster of its small leaves, a branchlet's worth, 0.26 m long, so that the crown keeps within the module limit; the seed plants' rules space the shoots from the card's area.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 4 m at 25 years and 7 m at 80. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: grey bark, grey-green leaves, lavender flowers. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): grey bark, smooth when young and shredding in strips when old; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): a pea flower: banner, two wings and keel between five sepals, ten stamens hidden in the keel, and one pistil, from the characters of Fabaceae and Olneya by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Desert Legume Program's page on the species, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): leaves once pinnate, mostly 3 to 6 cm long, with 6 to 16 small leaflets. The University of Arizona Campus Arboretum calls them even-pinnately compound, with obovate or elliptic leaflets; Virginia Tech Dendrology gives 6 to 9 pairs of obovate leaflets.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: The leaf drawn as a compound leaf (spec rework P4), its leaflets counted, set and shaped from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants and the plants (an even count: it ends in a pair); before, a fern's frond stood in for it. By eye from photographs: the leaflets 60 degrees from the rachis and a little under half as wide as long, so that they stand clear of each other.

generator.params.light_cell.note: The light grid's cells 0.4 m across, as the umbrella thorn's: with its leaves drawn as the compound leaves they are (spec rework P4), which shade twice what the frond did, 0.3 m cells let a seedling's own leaves shade it for decades (seed 2 stood at 0.64 m from its fifth year to past its 25th). A model setting, not a measurement.

generator.params.bloom_area.note: The area its `bloom` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms Skill 4, 2026-10-15; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: the bloom is now a raceme of its flowers, where before it drew one flower (0.259).

generator.params.bloom_size.note: Each bloom is a short raceme of pea flowers (Kearney and Peebles 1942, p. 466), as long as Abrams gives the racemes, 3 to 5 cm (vol. 2, 1944, p. 562), so 4 cm; its flowers are as wide as the corolla is long, 8 to 10 mm, by the cluster rules.
